text: I was two months into a GLP-1, dropping weight and still waking up every morning feeling backed up and uncomfortable like nothing had moved. Let me tell you what I finally found out because nobody told me about it either. Because I was dropping weight, the shot was actually working, but I felt like someone had filled my gut with concrete and forgotten about it. That heavy backed-up pressure that just sat there all day. I'd eat a few bites at dinner and feel like I'd swallowed a brick, and it didn't matter how little I ate. It just kept building. My jeans were getting looser, but I was still leaving the dinner table early because of how uncomfortable I felt. I'd stand in the kitchen after meals just waiting for it to pass, and I couldn't explain it to anyone without sounding like I was being dramatic. And I genuinely thought losing the weight would fix it. That was the thing. I believed if I just got the number down, the rest would follow. My doctor's advice was to add more fiber, so I did. I was mixing fiber powder into my water every morning, eating high-fiber everything, following every piece of advice she gave me. And I gave it real time, weeks, then a couple of months, and nothing really moved. I was still waking up every morning feeling like my gut was full of yesterday. So I went to the pharmacy and got Miralax, and that felt like a different kind of moment. That felt like admitting something had genuinely gone wrong. I was standing in that aisle thinking I shouldn't need this, but I was desperate enough that I didn't care anymore. I just wanted to feel okay. It helped a little, but the moment it wore off, I was right back where I started. Backed up, uncomfortable, just waiting. Something was definitely still missing. So I started doing a crazy amount of research on what was actually happening. I must have read thirty different articles, forums, medical breakdowns, all of it. And then I came across a gastroenterologist who had written out exactly what GLP-1 medications do to the gut. He explained it like this: your stomach is basically a muscle. It contracts, churns your food, and pushes everything forward. But GLP-1 medications slow those contractions down. Think of a river that suddenly slows to a trickle. Everything that was flowing through starts to back up behind it. Food backs up, waste backs up, gas builds with nowhere to go, and all that pressure is what you're feeling every single day. It wasn't a diet problem. It wasn't something I was doing wrong. It was the gut slowdown. So now I knew what was causing it, but I still had no idea what actually addressed the slowdown itself.
